Select your preferred package manager below to view installation instructions
for zen-do.

::: {.panel-tabset}
## Linux/macOS

To use the installer script, run this in the terminal:

```bash {filename="Terminal"}
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LsSf https://github.com/seedcase-project/zen-do/releases/latest/download/cargo-dist-installer.sh | sh
```

## Pixi

You can install zen-do as a [conda package on
Prefix.dev](https://prefix.dev/tools/repository) using
[Pixi](https://pixi.prefix.dev/latest/). You'll need to install Pixi if you
don't have it, after that, install zen-do globally with:

```bash {filename="Terminal"}
pixi global install --channel https://prefix.dev/seedcase yq
```

To update the globally installed packages, use:

```bash {filename="Terminal"}
pixi global update
```

## uv

::::: callout-tip
If you prefer to not install zen-do as a standalone command, you can use `uvx`
to install and run it in one step instead. To use `uvx` with zen-do, prefix the
command invocation with `uvx` each time you type out a zen do command:

```bash {filename="Terminal"}
uvx --from zen-do-cli zen-do --version
```
:::::

First, ensure you have [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv) installed. Then, install
zen-do from PyPI with:

```bash {filename="Terminal"}
uv tool install zen-do-cli
```

To upgrade zen-do with uv, you can run:

```bash {filename="Terminal"}
uv tool upgrade --all
```

## Cargo

First, ensure you have Rust and Cargo installed. If not, follow the [Rust
installation guide](https://rust-lang.org/tools/install/) which uses `rustup` to
install both. Then, install zen-do from [crates.io](https://crates.io) with:

```bash {filename="Terminal"}
cargo install zen-do
```

You can also install the binary directly (and more quickly) using
[cargo-binstall](https://github.com/cargo-bins/cargo-binstall). You will need
`cargo-binstall` to be installed.

```bash {filename="Terminal"}
cargo binstall zen-do
```

To upgrade zen-do with Cargo, you can rerun the installation command.

::::: callout-tip
If you can't run zen-do after installing it, check that the installation
directory is on your `PATH` as Cargo installs binary executables in the
following directory by default:

- **macOS or Linux:** `$HOME/.cargo/bin`
- **Windows:** `%USERPROFILE%\.cargo\bin`
:::::
:::

To confirm that zen-do was installed correctly, run:

```bash {filename="Terminal"}
zen-do --version
```

If the `zen-do` command cannot be found, try restarting your terminal.
